collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE II: THE LAND, MEMORY AND NEW TRADITIONS (LCB-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
Isola's ceremonies for the land and sea, its ways of remembering and mourning, and the new traditions its people make, question and change: rain songs, reef promises, memory gardens, funerals, forgotten melodies and festivals nobody planned.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A storm has broken the old memorial stone: restore it exactly, or rebuild it in a new way.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The storm last night knocked over the memorial stone at the edge of the village, and it cracked in two. (subject) wants it put back exactly as it was, crack and all. (friend) thinks this is a chance to make a new memorial, with the names of the people who have died since the stone was raised. What should the village do?

choices.label: Rebuild It in a New Way

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The village lifts the two halves and binds them together with rope and resin, crack and all. (subject) says the crack is part of its story now. (friend) carves the new names on a smaller stone beside it. Both stand there together.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The village builds a new memorial from the broken pieces, set in a circle, with all the names, old and new. Some of the elders are upset that it looks so different. Children like sitting in the middle of it.
